newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle steady at $67 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle steady at $67 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday were moderate at $67.00 per cwt, unchanged from the bulk of last week's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 6,000 head sold early in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, but further bids at $67.00 were being passed by several owners pricing cattle at $68.00, they said.

There were no reported sales in Kansas as bids at $67.00 were not dislodging cattle from owners who continue to ask $68.00, the feedlot sources said. Owners were holding tight to $68.00 asking levels amid ideas that packers would need cattle for early next week, the sources said.
Most beef processing plants will remain open during the upcoming Easter holiday weekend, company officials said.
One exception is Monfort Inc's plant in Dumas, Texas, which will be closed on Monday, according to K.T. Miller, a spokesperson for ConAgra Inc. Monfort is a unit of ConAgra.
Outlooks for firm fed beef prices also were generated by ideas beef demand would increase following the holiday weekend, market sources said.
Active beef movement on Wednesday reinforced projections for continued strong demand, however, packers had to lower prices to move beef out the door, they said.
